claire: Quick sync — we need a proposal for a private-offer structure that bundles Reserved Capacity + HW kickers with SI integration credits. Goal: make it easy for mid-market customers to commit, get partner margin, and have a clear renewal path. Thoughts?

raj: Love this. main ask: how do we avoid compounding discounts across Redwood and HW partner? we need caps and conversion mechanics. :thinking_face:

mia: Finance here — two initial constraints: 1) total stack discount (Redwood + HW + SI) max 30% off list. 2) renewal floor = 60% of year-1 effective spend to avoid revenue cliffs. can be relaxed for strategic deals with exec approval.

ethan: For sales/field: timeline matters. procurement cycles for HW are quarterly; customers expect renew/commit triggers 60d before term. we should push a 90d pre-renew notification and offer a conversion credit (one-time) if they upsell to next commit band. @claire

claire: Agreed on notification. Proposal idea: tranche the commit into 3 bands (onramp, steady, scale) with decreasing incremental discount, and a conversion credit applied at renewal if customer stays or increases. sample tiers:

```
Band A (0-25% commit): +5% Redwood discount, HW rebate 3%, SI credit $10k
Band B (25-60%): +12% Redwood discount, HW rebate 6%, SI credit $25k
Band C (60%+): +20% Redwood discount, HW rebate 10%, SI credit $50k
Total combined discount capped at 30%
Renewal conversion credit = min(10% of year-1 committed spend, $75k) applied once at renewal
```

sara: Legal flag: need to ensure rebates and credits don't create a back-to-back chargeback loop with marketplace invoicing. Also watch for regional procurement regs in EU (cannot tie HW purchase to cloud consumption in some GOV customers). will draft a simple clause.

devon: Product note — sku mapping: we should expose a single "commit package" SKU that maps to Redwood model SKUs + partner identifiers so billing and routing maintain observability. also telemetry hook to mark which requests came from commit traffic vs overage.

partner-bot: FYI: shared doc with HW partner templates uploaded -> https://redwood.internal/partnerships/mp-commit-templates (read-only) :white_check_mark:

raj: On renewal smoothing: can we offer a rolling 12-month average for overage calculations during year 1 and 2? reduces sticker shock and encourages adoption.

mia: rolling avg ok but we need a floor: never below 50% of committed monthly baseline for billing. also requires stricter monitoring for abuse.

ethan: Field ask: SI wants ability to earmark professional services as a separate line that counts toward conversion credits but not toward discount cap. can we do that?

claire: I like earmarking. operationally we can treat PS as "conversion credit sources" not discount sources. legal + finance to confirm.

sara: Confirming — PS can be treated as a non-discountable credit if invoiced separately by SI and clearly documented. will draft wording.

devon: Implementation notes: need a flag in the commit API: {"commit_band":"A|B|C","si_earmark_id":"..."} so we can attribute credits at billing time. minimal change but required.

claire: Next steps: 1) @mia finalize numeric cap floor/renewal credit calc by EOD Fri. 2) @sara draft marketplace-safe clause and SI-credit wording by Tues. 3) @devon & billing team prototype commit SKU & API flag (POC) by next Wed. 4) @ethan & @raj pilot with 2 HW partners and 3 target customers (mid-market) — kickoff next week.

raj: I'll line up partner contacts and draft partner-facing one-pager.

ethan: I'll prep the field playbook and timeline.

mia: Will push numbers and a brief spreadsheet with modeled AR impact.

sara: I'll drop a draft clause into the shared doc.

claire: Great — if no objections I'll send this as a proposal to HW partners and SI leads by EOD Monday. :rocket:

partner-bot: Action items created: 4 tasks assigned. Link: https://redwood.internal/tasks/MP-2777771234

claire: Thanks everyone — keeping thread here for transparency. ping me if you want to be added to pilot channel. :thumbsup:
